newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE's Vranitzky to urge outside help for Albania.
newsitem.headline: OSCE's Vranitzky to urge outside help for Albania.

text.p: European mediator Franz Vranitzky said on Friday he will urge the European Union and OSCE member states to give serious thought to a request from crisis-hit Albania to send in military support.

Vranitzky, speaking to Reuters by telephone from an Italian frigate in the Adriatic where he was holding talks with Albanian government leaders, said he believed order could only be restored in Albania with outside help.

Vranitzky said he would speak as soon as possible to Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo, whose country currently holds the EU presidency, and Denmark's Foreign Minister Niels Helveg Petersen, current chairman of the 54-member state Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE).
"I will urge them today, or at the latest tomorrow, to make a decision one way or the other," the former Austrian chancellor said.

"I think the OSCE and the EU countries should give it very thorough thought because this seems to be the most urgent answer the Albanians have to get, otherwise chaos and anarchy will continue," he added.

He said he was told by Prime Minister Bashkim Fino, Foreign Minister Arjan Starova and army chief of staff General Adem Copani that they could not cope with the situation by themselves. "They believe they can overcome it if there is support from abroad," Vranitzky said.
